- [LUNI.3.1.8] **A unit literal's numeric prefix is decimal. Hex, binary and
  octal prefixes are excluded**, and the exclusion is forced rather than
  chosen: the based form is **ambiguous with the integer literal it is built
  from**, provably and from the clause text alone.

  `[LLEX.11.1]` makes `_` an internal digit separator in `HEX_LIT`, and a
  `UNIT_SUFFIX` may be spelled entirely from characters that are also hex
  digits. Whenever it is, both productions match the same input at the same
  length:

  | input | as `HEX_LIT` | as a based unit literal |
  |---|---|---|
  | `0xFF_FF` | `0xFFFF` = 65535 | `0xFF` with unit `FF` |
  | `0xFF_A` | `0xFFA` = 4090 | `0xFF` with unit `A` — 255 amperes |

  **The two readings are opposite and a lexer has one priority ordering**, so
  either setting is wrong for one of these rows. `A` is the SI symbol for the
  ampere; the collision is not contrived on either side.

  `0xFF_FF` is the spelling the numeric-literal examples use and `[LLEX.11.1]`
  grants it directly, so any resolution reading it as a unit literal breaks a
  documented integer form.

  A decimal prefix has no such overlap: `DEC_LIT` admits no letters, so no
  `UNIT_SUFFIX` can continue it.
